title: MCP Tools for Todo Management
description: Model Context Protocol tool definitions for AI-powered todo CRUD operations. These tools are invoked by the OpenAI agent based on natural language user intent.

tools.name: add_todo
tools.description: Create a new todo item for the authenticated user. Use this when the user expresses intent to add, create, or remember a task. Extract the task title from the user's message and optionally include additional details as description.

title.description: The todo title describing what needs to be done. Should be concise and actionable (e.g., 'Buy groceries', 'Call mom', 'Finish project report').

description.description: Optional additional details or context about the todo. Use this for clarifications, deadlines mentioned in conversation, or other relevant information.

success.description: Whether the todo was created successfully

todo_id.description: ID of the created todo (present only on success)

title.description: The created todo's title (present only on success)

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code (present only on failure)

tools.error_handling: If title is empty or exceeds 200 characters, return validation_error. If database operation fails, return database_error with user-friendly message. Never expose internal error details to the AI.

tools.name: list_todos
tools.description: Retrieve all todos for the authenticated user. Use this when the user asks to see their tasks, what they need to do, or wants a list of todos. Optionally filter by completion status.

completed.description: Optional filter. If true, return only completed todos. If false, return only incomplete todos. If omitted, return all todos.

todos.description: List of todos (present only on success)

total.description: Total number of todos returned (present only on success)

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code (present only on failure)

tools.error_handling: If database query fails, return database_error. Always enforce user isolation (todos filtered by authenticated user_id).

tools.name: complete_todo
tools.description: Mark a todo as completed. Use this when the user indicates they've finished a task, want to mark something as done, or check off an item.

todo_id.description: The ID of the todo to mark as complete. Must belong to the authenticated user.
ID of the completed todo (present only on success)

title.description: Title of the completed todo (present only on success)

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code (present only on failure)

output.message: Todo not found or does not belong to you

tools.error_handling: Return not_found if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user (enforce user isolation). Return already_completed if todo is already marked complete (informational, not an error). Return authorization_error if user attempts to complete another user's todo.

tools.name: update_todo
tools.description: Update a todo's title, description, or completion status. Use this when the user wants to modify, change, rename, or edit an existing todo.

todo_id.description: The ID of the todo to update. Must belong to the authenticated user.

title.description: New title for the todo (optional, if omitted, title remains unchanged)

description.description: New description for the todo (optional, if omitted, description remains unchanged)

completed.description: New completion status (optional, if omitted, status remains unchanged). Use complete_todo tool for simple completion.

todo.description: Updated todo object (present only on success)

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code (present only on failure)

output.message: Todo not found or does not belong to you

tools.error_handling: Return not_found if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user. Return validation_error if title is empty or exceeds limits. Return authorization_error if user attempts to update another user's todo. At least one field (title, description, or completed) must be provided.

tools.name: delete_todo
tools.description: Permanently delete a todo. Use this when the user wants to remove, delete, or get rid of a task. Confirm with user before deletion if intent is ambiguous.

todo_id.description: The ID of the todo to delete. Must belong to the authenticated user.
ID of the deleted todo (present only on success)

title.description: Title of the deleted todo (present only on success)

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code (present only on failure)

output.message: Todo not found or does not belong to you

tools.error_handling: Return not_found if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user (enforce user isolation). Return authorization_error if user attempts to delete another user's todo. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

user_isolation.description: All MCP tools MUST enforce user isolation at the execution level. The authenticated user_id (from JWT token) is injected into tool execution context and is NOT provided by the AI as a parameter. Tools validate that requested resources (todo_id) belong to the authenticated user before performing operations.
user_isolation.enforcement: Repository layer filters all queries by user_id. Authorization failures return 403 Forbidden with error_code 'authorization_error'.

input_validation.description: All tool parameters are validated using Pydantic models before execution. Invalid inputs return structured error responses with validation_error code.
validation_rules: todo_id: positive integer (required for complete, update, delete)
completed: boolean (optional for list_todos and update_todo)

error_responses.description: All tools return structured responses with success boolean, message string, and optional error_code. Error messages are user-friendly and do not expose internal implementation details.
error_codes: not_found: Requested resource does not exist or does not belong to user
authorization_error: User is not authorized to access the resource
already_completed: Todo is already marked as complete (informational)
database_error: Database operation failed (transient or persistent)

implementation_notes.async_execution: All MCP tools must be implemented as async Python functions to integrate with FastAPI's async event loop.
implementation_notes.transaction_handling: Database operations should use transactions to ensure consistency. Rollback on any error.
implementation_notes.logging: All tool invocations must be logged with user_id, tool_name, parameters, and result for audit trail.
implementation_notes.performance: Target execution time: <500ms per tool invocation (per spec NFR).
implementation_notes.openai_integration: These tool definitions are converted to OpenAI function calling format and registered with the Assistant. The AI decides when to invoke each tool based on user intent.
